item.title: How voice AI is transforming banking and insurance: Desible.ai founders on the business behind the technology
item.description: In this episode of the Prime Venture Partners Podcast, Gaurav Ranjan sits down with Uttam and Omkar to discuss what it takes to build and sell agentic AI in Indian BFSI, from product engineering and compliance to enterprise sales and scaling beyond the first use case.
item.content:encoded:
In this episode of the Prime Venture Partners Podcast, Gaurav Ranjan sits down with Uttam and Omkar to discuss what it takes to build and sell agentic AI in Indian BFSI, from product engineering and compliance to enterprise sales and scaling beyond the first use case.

From Rs 7 per minute to under Rs 2, voice AI is rapidly becoming cheaper. But Desible.ai co-founders Uttam Tiwari and Omkar Raikar believe the real opportunity lies beyond conversations, in automating the workflows that run large enterprises.

Building a voice AI agent that sounds human is no longer the hardest part of the problem. Getting that agent to operate reliably inside a bank or insurance company, navigate regulatory requirements, integrate with legacy systems and deliver measurable business outcomes is an entirely different challenge.

For Uttam Tiwari and Omkar Raikar, co-founders of Desible.ai, this distinction is shaping how they build their company. Desible is developing an agentic workflow orchestration platform for regulated enterprises, with an initial focus on insurance.

Speaking with Gaurav Ranjan, Principal at Prime Venture Partners, on the Prime Venture Partners Podcast, the founders discussed why AI pilots frequently fail to reach production, how enterprise buying behaviour is changing and why the economics of voice AI could fundamentally reshape the contact centre industry.

From 25 people to three: The moment that changed everything

Uttam and Omkar have known each other for 17 years. Their previous venture, Business Toys, was acquired in 2023, following which they worked with US enterprises, including Newsweek, Bank of America and Nestlé, through a software consulting and AI business.

The turning point came during a logistics brokerage project involving AI-powered calls to truckers for availability checks and verification. Following the implementation, the client restructured a contact centre of approximately 20 to 25 people to just three.

The experience demonstrated the potential of voice AI to change how enterprises operated. But as the founders explored the Indian market through proof-of-concept projects with 12 to 13 enterprises, they realised that automating conversations alone would not create a sufficiently differentiated business.

"Voice is a commodity. I do agree, but at the same time, workflows are not because workflow goes and sit deep inside organizational processes and that's where you get the moat," Uttam explained.

That insight led Desible to focus on insurance, where customer conversations are closely connected to renewals, persistency, claims, sales and servicing workflows.

Why AI demos succeed but production deployments fail

One of the most revealing discussions centred on the difference between demonstrating AI capabilities and deploying them inside regulated enterprises.

Uttam estimates that the conversion of proofs of concept into production deployments across the companies he has observed is below 35–40%. A successful demonstration, he argued, is only the beginning of a much more complicated journey.

Insurance companies require vendors to satisfy business teams, technology departments, information security teams, compliance functions and senior technology leadership before allowing systems into production.

Omkar described Indian information security reviews involving approximately 450 questions, including requirements around data residency and compute infrastructure. Even established international technology providers can struggle with these requirements.

Desible consequently invested much of its initial funding into building compliant infrastructure rather than concentrating exclusively on voice capabilities.

For Omkar, consistency is particularly important because insurance conversations leave little room for improvisation.

"You need to be speaking the same boring language every single time, staying compliant."

The technical challenges extend beyond compliance. Voice agents must manage interruptions, understand multilingual conversations, retrieve information from enterprise systems and respond appropriately without losing context.

In one example, Omkar explained how an AI agent conducting a medical questionnaire must recognise when a customer interrupts before hearing the complete question. In another, the system must identify a medicine mentioned during a conversation, verify it against a database and ask the appropriate follow-up question.

These capabilities distinguish a production-ready system from a conversational demonstration.

The economics of Voice AI are changing rapidly

The pricing of voice AI has undergone a dramatic shift. As Gaurav highlighted during the discussion, traditional human contact centre operations can cost approximately ₹20–₹30 per minute, while early voice AI solutions were priced at Rs 5–Rs 7 per minute.

Competitive pricing has since fallen to approximately Rs 1.5–Rs 3 per minute.

For startups building voice AI products, this creates an uncomfortable question: if the underlying technology keeps becoming cheaper, how can they capture a meaningful share of the value they create?

Omkar argued that per-minute pricing was never the natural economic model for contact centres, which historically charged based on seats or headcount. The emergence of voice AI introduced a pricing structure based on infrastructure and API consumption.

Desible is attempting to move beyond this model by charging for workflow execution rather than treating each call as an isolated transaction.

The company is already handling close to a million calls daily, according to Omkar. He also described how Desible has reduced its underlying call execution costs from approximately Rs 7–Rs 8 using earlier approaches to below Rs 1.5–Rs 2 through its orchestration capabilities.

However, the founders acknowledge that enterprise customers are still evaluating whether AI delivers sustainable returns.

Uttam shared an example of a customer that did not renew three small regional contact centres after Desible's solution had been running for approximately four and a half months.

The broader transition, he cautioned, remains gradual because enterprises need sustained operational evidence before reallocating budgets.

Enterprise buyers no longer care only about human-like voices

A year earlier, enterprise customers primarily evaluated voice AI through parameters such as latency, tone, language switching and how naturally an agent sounded.

That evaluation has changed. Today, Uttam explained, customers increasingly compare AI systems directly with human employees on contactability, conversion rates, lead qualification and the accuracy of information recorded after conversations.

The shift from technological novelty to measurable operational performance is also changing how Desible approaches enterprise sales.

Rather than pursuing every potential AI experiment, the company prioritises workflows that already exist within an organisation. Such processes have established owners, operating procedures, budgets and performance benchmarks, making it easier to demonstrate the value of automation.

"Your champion may not be your buyer," Uttam cautioned.

A business leader enthusiastic about an AI pilot may still lack the authority to approve deployment. Information security, technology, compliance and procurement teams can all influence the final decision.

For founders selling enterprise AI, identifying these stakeholders early can be as important as building the product itself.

In India, enterprise sales is as much about navigation as technology

Perhaps the most striking observation came when Gaurav asked whether enterprise sales was 40% product and 60% navigating internal organisational dynamics.

Omkar suggested that in India, the latter could account for as much as 80%.

Even a technically superior product, he argued, may fail without the ability to understand decision-making structures, secure internal support and sustain relationships across multiple stakeholders.

Desible's expansion strategy illustrates the approach. At one insurance customer, the company began with sales funnel management before expanding into welcome calls, persistency and inbound customer servicing.

Each successful workflow creates additional trust and reduces the effort required for subsequent integrations. Within insurance renewals alone, the company has identified more than 20 distinct workflows.

The founders believe that this combination of industry specialisation, compliance readiness and integration into existing enterprise processes creates a more durable advantage than voice quality alone.

Beyond voice: Building an operating system for insurance

Despite the competitive intensity surrounding voice AI, Omkar believes the market remains underexplored, particularly in India, where multiple languages, dialects, background noise and frequent language switching make conversational systems considerably more challenging.

He believes companies that solve these problems at scale could emerge as global leaders.

For Desible, however, the long-term ambition extends beyond handling calls. The founders envision an orchestration platform that supports insurance companies and intermediaries, including third-party administrators, brokers and health aggregators, across their operational workflows.

The ultimate measure of success will not be how convincingly an AI agent speaks, but whether it helps enterprises make better decisions, improve customer outcomes and operate more efficiently.

Uttam's assessment of where the industry currently stands captures the central lesson for AI founders:

"POC is overhyped but production is underhyped."

As enterprises move from experimenting with AI to demanding measurable results, the winners may not be the companies with the most impressive demonstrations, but those capable of turning AI into dependable infrastructure for everyday business operations.

item.title: Health, sustainability, AI: test your business creativity with Edition 256 of our weekly quiz!
item.description: This insightful feature from YourStory tests and strengthens your business acumen! Here are 5 questions to kick off this 256th quiz. Ready?
item.content:encoded:
Lateral Sparks, the weekly quiz from YourStory, tests your domain knowledge, business acumen, and lateral thinking skills (see the previous edition here). In this 256th edition of the quiz, we present issues tackled by real-life entrepreneurs in their startup journeys.

What would you do if you were in their shoes? At the end of the quiz, you will find out what the entrepreneurs and innovators themselves actually did. Would you do things differently?

Check out YourStory’s Book Review section as well, with takeaways from over 355 titles on creativity and entrepreneurship, and our weekend PhotoSparks section on creativity in the arts.

Also Read
How IIT Madras Incubation Cell is powering India’s next-gen deeptech startups

Q1: Workflow

Frontline workforce management is ripe for transformation by AI, but is often underserved in enterprise digital initiatives. How can this gap be addressed?

Q2: Rural healthcare

Many remote rural areas suffer from healthcare problems due to lack of access to clinicians. Just an app will not help here – what is a more effective solution?

Q3: Travel

Travel planning by organisations continues to be plagued with issues like changing prices and shifting itineraries. How can technology help here?

Also Read
Year in review: What 2025’s data tells us about women in India

Q4: Flowers

Many rural areas are blessed with a plentiful range of flowers. How can the flower market here be enabled for customers across the country, even when the products are fragile and perish quickly?

Q5: Waste processing

Large volumes of non-recyclable dry waste are being generated in cities every day, leading to problems for municipal collection systems. How can this problem be tackled?

Answers!

Congratulations on having come this far! But there’s more to come – answers to these five questions (below), as well as links to articles with more details on the entrepreneurs’ solutions. Happy reading, happy learning – and happy creating!

A1: Workflow

Founded by Krishna Khandelwal and Shantanu Bhattacharyya, Hunar.AI offers specialised AI technology for frontline-intensive industries. It helps HR teams who struggle with high-volume hiring, geographically distributed teams, and language diversity.

It has developed conversational AI for candidate sourcing and screening, employee engagement, and worker retention. Read more here about its clients such as Swiggy, Delhivery, Pronto, Blue Dart, Flipkart, Aditya Birla Capital, and Tata Croma.

A2: Rural healthcare

Founded by Priyadarshi Mohapatra, Shobhan Mahapatra and Sanjay Swain, CureBay operates a technology-enabled rural healthcare network. It combines physical clinics with digital services, via IoT-enablement, AI-powered screening, and a 24/7 command centre.

“Rural Bharat doesn’t need another app; it needs a system that works end to end,” says Priyadarshi Mohapatra. Read more here about how it operates more than 250 technology-enabled clinics across seven states, serving over 17 lakh patients.

Also Read
Year in Review: Top 10 celebrity-backed ventures of 2025

A3: Travel

Founded by Arun Bagaria, traveltech startup TravClan is building infrastructure that travel businesses can use instead of having to recreate the entire travel stack. It enables travel agents to plan, price and rebuild complex international itineraries in a shorter period of time.

It leverages AI to bring global inventory, booking, and destination fulfillment into one platform. Read more here about how it has 15,000 travel agents as customers, processing more than $100 million in annual travel sales.

A4: Flowers

Founded by Chokhone Krichena, Dianthe takes Manipur’s distinctive flowers to customers across India while helping rural women earn an income. Value is added by drying the flowers for preserving their beauty, and giving longer shelf-life to flowers such as geraniums and hydrangeas.

“Everything is naturally preserved. We shade-dry them and for a few varieties, we sun-dry them,” the ‘Flower Lady of Manipur’ describes. Read more here about how her organisation also uses baskets woven by women’s self-help groups, and eco-friendly wraps instead of plastic.

Also Read
Year in review: startups that raised big from VCs in 2025

A5: Waste processing

Founded by Dhwaj Bagrecha, Neo San processes non-recyclable waste right at the location where it is generated. It has built compact thermal processing units for dry reject, sanitary, and biomedical waste, reducing the need to transport it to distant disposal sites.

This Tech30 startup uses rapid, high-temperature electric heating based on induction, which reduces waste to sterile, non-toxic ash. Read more here about its Neo-X wall-mounted unit for washrooms, and Neo-XT for tech parks, small hospitals, and commercial complexes.

YourStory has also published the pocketbook ‘Proverbs and Quotes for Entrepreneurs: A World of Inspiration for Startups’ as a creative and motivational guide for innovators.

item.title: EKA Mobility expands manufacturing footprint
item.description: The company said the six plants in Pune and Pithampur are part of an 11-facility network spread across 120 acres, with annual capacity for more than 40,000 electric vehicles and investment exceeding Rs 3,500 crore.
item.content:encoded:
Electric mobility firm EKA Mobility has inaugurated six manufacturing facilities across Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh in a bid to scale production of electric buses, trucks and smaller commercial vehicles as India expands fleet electrification. 

The company said the six plants in Pune and Pithampur are part of a 11-facility network spread across 120 acres, with annual capacity for more than 40,000 electric vehicles and investment exceeding Rs 3,500 crore. The facilities cover vehicle assembly, engineering, battery enclosures, seating and interiors.

EKA claims 1,243% year-on-year growth in H1 FY27. It also asserts an order book of more than 11,000 buses. 

Founder and Chairman Sudhir Mehta emphasised the importance of affordability and accessibility, saying, “Until we make it accessible and affordable for all, we will not have achieved our vision, and no amount of technology matters if it does not reach the people who depend on it every day.”

Competition, however, is intensifying. VAHAN-based figures show that India registered 2,944 electric buses between January and June 2026, a 40% increase year-on-year. Switch Mobility led with 830 registrations, followed by JBM Auto with 635 and PMI Electro Mobility with 574. Pinnacle Mobility Solutions, the company behind EKA, registered 171, accounting for 5.8% of the market.

Meanwhile, Government policy is supporting this expansion. The PM E-DRIVE scheme, whose outlay increased to Rs 11,900 crore in August 2026, earmarks Rs 4,391 crore for 14,028 electric buses and Rs 500 crore for 5,643 electric trucks. The scheme has been extended for most segments until March 2028. 

A separate PM-eBus Sewa payment-security programme supports the deployment of more than 38,000 buses, addressing concerns around delayed payments to operators. The Rs 25,938-crore production-linked incentive programme also seeks to strengthen domestic advanced automotive technology manufacturing.

item.title: Atomberg Technologies receives SEBI nod for IPO
item.description: The proceeds of the IPO will be used for repayment of debt, branding & marketing and R&D.
item.content:encoded:
Consumer appliance maker Atomberg Technologies has received the approval from Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) for its initial public offering (IPO).

The IPO will be a combination of fresh issue of shares and offer for sale. Atomberg plans to raise Rs 450 crore through the fresh issue of shares and an offer for sale of 76,542,051 equity shares of face value Rs 10 each.

The company proposes to utilise the proceeds from the IPO towards debt payment, investments into brand awareness & marketing, R&D and general corporate purposes.

Atomberg reported a revenue of Rs 1293.77 crore for FY26 as compared to Rs 959.51 crore recorded in FY25, registering a growth of 34.83%. It reported a loss of Rs 148.88 crore for FY26.

Founded in 2012, Atomberg manufactures a range of consumer appliances which include mixer grinders, water purifiers and cold-pressed juicers. The company also designs, manufactures and supplies proprietary and critical components, including motors and controllers, to enterprise customers such as Voltas, Godrej and BlueStar.

Atomberg sells its products through an omni-channel distribution model spanning offline channels such as general trade distributors, retailers, modern trade chains and institutional partners, and online channels including e-commerce marketplaces, quick-commerce platforms and its own website.

Its revenue from online channels increased to Rs 456.45 crore in FY2026 from Rs 234.51 crores in FY2024, while offline channel revenue rose to Rs 820.11 Crores from Rs 562.47 crores over the same period. The online channel contributed approximately 35.76% of the revenue from the consumer appliances business.

Atomberg operates two leased manufacturing facilities in Pune, Maharashtra, supporting its consumer appliances and proprietary components businesses. Its Chakan facility in Pune, which commenced operations in FY2022 manufactures ceiling fans, table, pedestal and wall fans, exhaust fans, mixer grinders, cold-pressed juicers and smart locks.

item.title: [Weekly funding roundup Oct 24-30] VC inflow continues to remain modest
item.description: The inflow of venture capital into Indian startups remained lukewarm for the month of October and this trend was reflected in the last week also.
item.content:encoded:
Venture capital funding into Indian startups remained subdued in October, primarily due to the absence of large-value deals.

There was not a single deal worth more than $100 million during the month, while weekly funding remained below $200 million.

The last week of October saw total funding of $115 million across 29 deals, compared with $96 million in VC inflows during the previous week.

The largest deal of the week was a $15 million investment in healthtech startup Cent. Despite 29 transactions during the week, large-value deals remained absent.

Interestingly, two of the deals involved pure-play AI startups, a number that is expected to grow in the coming months.

As the year draws to a close, venture capital inflows into Indian startups are unlikely to differ significantly from 2025 levels. This underscores the challenges the ecosystem continues to face in attracting large volumes of capital, partly due to the lack of a strong AI investment story in the country.

The expectation is that 2027 could bring a turnaround.

Key transactions

Healthtech startup Cent raised $15 million from Blume Ventures, South Park Commons, and angel investors.

AI inference infrastructure startup Simplismart raised $14 million from Dallas Venture Capital, NVIDIA, Accel, Shastra VC and Micromax.

AI startup Live2 ai raised Rs 130 crore ($14 million approx.) led by IvyCap Ventures.

Food and snacks brand Troovy raised Rs 100 crore ($10.4 million approx.) from Fireside Ventures, Sharrp Ventures and other investors.

Social gaming platform Matiks raised $10 million from General Catalyst, Ronnie Screwvala, Info Edge Ventures, Tanglin Venture Partners, and Untitled Ventures.

Nutrition products company Ace Blend raised $9.91 million from 3one4 Capital and Fireside Ventures.

Luxury watchmaker Rotoris raised Rs 70 crore ($8.5 million approx.) from Blume Ventures, 9Unicorns, Centricity and angel investors.

item.title: Design and experience: How Essensai 067 crafts an open-air lifestyle and community destination
item.description: In this photo essay from Whitefield, we showcase design highlights from Essensai 067 along with founder insights.
item.content:encoded:
Launched in 2014, PhotoSparks is a weekly feature from YourStory, with photographs that celebrate the spirit of creativity and innovation. In the earlier 1,030 posts, we featured an art festival, cartoon gallery. world music festival, telecom expo, millets fair, climate change expo, wildlife conference, startup festival, Diwali rangoli, and jazz festival.

Does every large retail destination in a rapidly growing city have to be like a multi-storeyed air-conditioned mall? Essensai 067 in Whitefield does not believe so, and has found a unique positioning as an open-air lifestyle and community destination.

As shown in this photo essay, it combines dining, entertainment, shopping, wellness, and culture in a green and spacious setting Visitors can enjoy landscaped spaces and relaxed outdoor experiences rather than spending their time inside a boxed mall.

The space is also pet-friendly, unlike many other retail destinations and dining areas. The artworks and design encourage people to slow down and enjoy quality time, with a notable focus on sustainability, culture and community engagement.

Natural landscaping, solar energy, and climate-sensitive design send out subtle messages about environmental protection as well. The amphitheatre and open gathering spaces are host to live music, cultural performances, exhibitions, flea markets, and other community events.

Event programming has included garba nights, Christmas carnivals, qawaali, open-air movie nights, and pop-up markets. There was even a Kidzeprenuer Flea Market, where children aged 6–14 ran their own stalls over two days.

Also Read
Year in Review: The great Indian consumer reset powered by protein, pickleball and micro-dramas

“The enthusiastic community response reinforces our belief that programming can give a neighbourhood destination a life beyond shopping and dining. Success is not just about how many people show up on a particular evening, but in how they begin to see the space as part of their own neighbourhood routine,” Haresh Mirpuri. MD of Sai Lakshmi Industries and Creative Director of Essensai 067, tells YourStory.

Interestingly, the name of the space is derived from a combination of the words essence, Sai Lakshmi Industries, Sai Baba, and the 067 postal code of the Whitefield neighbourhood.

“Whitefield has grown rapidly in terms of homes and offices. We felt there was an opportunity to create a different kind of neighbourhood experience: somewhere you could go for a morning walk, sit with a coffee, take a class, discover something being made, meet friends without making elaborate plans, or simply spend time outdoors,” Mirpuri observes.

That was the starting point for Essensai 067. “We wanted to bring nature, art, community and craft into the same conversation as local and international food, retail, wellness, and entertainment. These are not separate attractions assembled under one roof; they are different parts of how people want to live,” he adds.

As trends in retail and lifestyle, he points to the growing expectation for engaging experiences, variations in weekday and weekend activities, and active citizen participation. “People increasingly want to do something, learn something, meet the person behind a product, or become part of an experience,” Mirpuri describes.

“We designed the district to feel thoughtfully put together – offering commercial vitality, but also with a clear point of view. Curation matters as much as the individual offering,” he affirms.

Also Read
Year in Review: Top 10 celebrity-backed ventures of 2025

A space is defined not just by its architecture or layout. “Its character develops through the people who visit, the brands and makers who become part of it, the experiences that take root, and the habits that form over time,” he adds.

“Any future location would need its own local understanding, programming and identity. The thinking should travel; the experience itself must belong to the neighbourhood,” Mirpuri explains, while referring to next steps.

In sum, Essensai 067 is aiming to build a destination that feels as dynamic and engaging as the city itself, while retaining the ease, openness and sense of familiarity of a neighbourhood space.

Mirpuri also offers tips for aspiring entrepreneurs in retail, food and entertainment. “Before deciding what a space should contain, understand who lives around it, how they spend their time, what they travel elsewhere for, and what is missing from their everyday lives,” he says.

“Build frequency before fame. It is easy to focus on a launch, a large event or a moment of visibility. The harder and more valuable task is giving people reasons to return,” he adds.

Curation can be more impactful than scale. “Not every destination needs the largest assortment or the most brands. It needs a clear point of view about what belongs there and why,” Mirpuri explains.

Also Read
Breaking barriers in 2025: Women’s progress at work and what the road ahead demands

“Finally, allow the people you work with to retain their identity. Independent brands, artists, makers, and experience partners bring their own communities and points of view. The role of the destination is to host, curate and enable them—not flatten everything into a single house style,” he says.

In experience-led businesses, the physical space is only the beginning. “What matters is the relationship that develops between the place, its partners and the people who return to it. That relationship is built through consistency, listening and a willingness to keep evolving,” Mirpuri signs off.

Now what have you done today to pause in your busy schedule and harness your creative side for a better world?

(All photographs taken by Madanmohan Rao on location at Essensai 067.)

item.title: Prosus investment in Sachin Bansal's Navi gets CCI nod
item.description: CCI has approved Prosus’ proposal to acquire a stake in Navi Ltd, following the fintech firm’s $100 million fundraise from the Dutch investment group in August. The deal will deepen Prosus’ presence in India’s digital financial services sector.
item.content:encoded:
Competition watchdog CCI has approved Dutch investment group Prosus' proposal to acquire a stake in Sachin Bansal-led fintech firm Navi Ltd, paving the way for the investment group to deepen its presence in India's digital financial services sector.

"The proposed combination involves the acquisition of certain shareholding in Navi Ltd (target) by MIH Payments Holdings BV (acquirer)," the regulator said in a release.

The Competition Commission of India (CCI) said it has approved the proposed deal.

MIH Payments Holdings BV does not undertake any business activity other than holding investments in its portfolio companies, which operate in India, the watchdog added.

Prosus is a global consumer internet group and one of the world's largest technology investors. It is majority-owned by the South African multinational mass media company Naspers.

Bengaluru-based Navi is the holding company of the Navi Group, founded by Bansal in 2018 after leaving Flipkart following its sale to Walmart.

The fintech firm provides a range of financial services, including digital payments, lending, insurance, and mutual funds.

In August, Navi announced that it had raised $100 million from Prosus, marking the company's first institutional capital raise and strengthening its position as it looks to scale its digital financial services businesses.

Deals beyond a certain threshold need regulatory approval, which monitors unfair business practices and promotes fair competition in the marketplace.

item.title: Jio Platforms’ first post-listing results: User growth, higher ARPU drive 13.7% profit rise in Q2
item.description: The digital and telecom company's consolidated revenue from operations rose 11.4% to Rs 40,475 crore during the quarter under review.
item.content:encoded:
Jio Platforms on Friday reported a 13.7% rise in consolidated net profit to Rs 8,389 crore for the September 2026 quarter, driven by subscriber gains, higher realisations per user and healthy growth in digital services.

The digital and telecom company's consolidated revenue from operations rose 11.4% to Rs 40,475 crore during the quarter under review, according to a regulatory filing.

The September-quarter scorecard is the company's first since its stellar listing earlier this week, and the earnings briefing also marks the first time Managing Director Akash Ambani addressed investors on a quarterly results call.

Commenting on the results, he said the reported quarter’s results continue to reflect the strength of the company's 5G network, and the growing reach of broadband and digital services".

"We would continue to build our capabilities across satellite communications, 6G intellectual property and AI embedded in our core voice and data services as we create lasting value for all our stakeholders," he said

During the results briefing, Ambani outlined Jio’s growth strategy ranging from international business models to opportunities in the enterprise segment by leveraging the technology stack built by the company and infrastructure laid out by it.

"Multiple growth engines across mobility, home, enterprise and international that we see. And again, we are the ones that are proving this at scale. We are the ones that have a clear path of growth and profitability improving with a very, very strong balance sheet, even before the IPO proceeds come to us,” Ambani said.

Net profit attributable to owners of the company stood at Rs 8,389 crore for the just-ended quarter against Rs 7,379 crore in the year-ago period.

On a sequential basis, consolidated net profit rose 8% from Rs 7,765 crore in the June quarter, while revenue from operations increased 3.3% from Rs 39,173 crore.

Ambani said the enterprise segment will be a major growth opportunity where it plans to double down and churn users towards the company’s network.

"The small and medium businesses that are existing in our country are a unique opportunity. We will be very, very selective about the international markets that we will go to. We will not be selling our proprietary stacks as a hardware commission or our software as a service. What we imagine the business model here to be is to be an actually managed service partner with our customers," he said.

The company’s net debt dropped 78.6% to Rs 8,822 crore in the reported quarter from Rs 41,161 a year ago.

Jio Platforms attributed the revenue growth to subscriber additions, higher average revenue per user (ARPU) and healthy growth in digital services.

Revenue from connectivity grew 11%, while digital services registered 16% growth during the quarter. The company's total subscriber base rose 7.1% to 54.24 crore from 50.64 crore a year earlier, with net additions of 91 lakh subscribers during the September quarter.

Monthly ARPU (average revenue per user) rose to Rs 218.8 from Rs 211.4 in the year-ago period and Rs 215.6 in the June quarter; average monthly data consumption per user increased 14.2% to 44.2 GB.

Jio also crossed the milestone of 30 crore 5G subscribers during the quarter, adding 6.6 crore 5G users over the past 12 months.

"Customer engagement also remained robust with 5G now accounting for nearly 56% of total wireless traffic," the JPL earnings release said.

The fixed broadband subscriber base touched 3 crore.

"Jio AirFiber with total base of 15.1 million subscribers, has driven more than

75% of Jio’s fixed broadband additions during the last 12 months," the release said.

Total data traffic rose 22.1% year-on-year to 71.3 billion GB during the quarter.

This is the first results announcement of the digital and telecom company after its blockbuster stock market debut earlier this week, when the company's shares ended nearly 27% above its Rs 1,119 issue price, making what was a telecom and digital upstart in 2016 the second-most valuable domestic firm by market capitalisation, in a matter of just 10 years.

The company's IPO raised Rs 30,188 crore, of which Rs 27,500 crore has been utilised towards prepayment of certain external commercial borrowings of its subsidiary Reliance Jio Infocomm.

Speaking at the JPL earnings call, Ambani said Jio Platforms' blockbuster initial public offering (IPO) broke records across all investor categories despite challenging market conditions and foreign outflows, and asserted that the company expects to create even greater value over the next decade than it did in its first ten years.

"We believe that the value we can create over the next decade or so is even greater than what we have created in our first decade," he said, adding that the company continues to aspire for more.

Reiterating the message from his NSE listing speech, Ambani said, "Never let today's achievement limit tomorrow's ambition, and that is what we want to carry forward with Jio".

Jio Platforms CEO Pankaj Panwar said the company is not bundling services in its offering but creating new market and value from customers, which is increasing wallet share for the company.

item.title: This art festival reveals why the creative economy is as much about audiences as creators
item.description: In this photo essay, we showcase more highlights from the Contemporary Now arts festival in Chennai, along with director insights.
item.content:encoded:
Launched in 2014, PhotoSparks is a weekly feature from YourStory, with photographs that celebrate the spirit of creativity and innovation. In the earlier 1,025 posts, we featured an art festival, cartoon gallery. world music festival, telecom expo, millets fair, climate change expo, wildlife conference, startup festival, Diwali rangoli, and jazz festival.

Chennai recently hosted the third edition of the art festival 'Contemporary Now', with collaboration from art galleries of Kolkata, Ahmedabad, New Delhi, and Mumbai as well. A diverse range of artworks was exhibited in 10 venues across the city, as shown in this photo essay.

The artist lineup included Ashwini Bhat, Prajakta Potnis, Khageswar Rout, Amitesh Shrivastava, Sandeep Mukherjee, Saju Kunhan, Pratap Morey, Benitha Perciyal, Natasha Preenja, and many others.

Also Read
2026 Outlook: AI, robotics, biotech, unicorns and the road ahead

“Now is a good time to be in art. Aspiring artists as well as audiences today are much more connected to art, thanks to social media,” mixed-media artist Benitha Perciyal tells YourStory.

Earlier, art catalogues and visits to a few galleries were the only available options. “You had to simply wait to get access and exposure, or travel to other cities, which was quite expensive,” she recalls.

“Today, online access is immediate and global. But at the same time, too much online exposure can be confusing or intimidating,” she cautions.

Also Read
Year in review: startups that raised big from VCs in 2025

Digital platforms and AI make things much easier and faster now for art. “But it also takes away from the satisfaction of finding or creating something after a lot of effort,” Perciyal says.

The art festival’s directors are Ashvin Rajagopalan and Priyanjoli Basu. Both express satisfaction with the event’s achievements for the art community of Chennai and beyond.

“We had collectors who usually have not come out much, but engaged with us at the festival. We had many art fans and students who could see what was happening in the rest of the country thanks to our institutional partners in other cities,” Rajagopalan says.

There are plans to have more editions of the festival. “We may end up having two or three editions of Contemporary Now. One, of course, in Chennai, but others could be in Ahmedabad, Baroda or Shantiniketan,” he adds.

“The festival’s level of contemporary artwork has probably not been shown in Chennai earlier. A lot of feedback I got was that there are major art events in Delhi and Mumbai but not as much in Chennai,” Basu observes.

The art community felt this event should happen more often in Chennai. “It should not be a once-a-year thing. The displayed artworks should be shown elsewhere also, to continue the conversation,” she adds.

Also Read
How IIT Madras Incubation Cell is powering India’s next-gen deeptech startups

As trends in the art market in India today, she points to more appreciation of art about politics, gender and climate change. “People are trying to engage with a new narrative, a new trend. The works of a lot of young women artists are also being collected,” Basu says.

“Many contemporary artists have been responding to what is happening around the world. Art collectors are also responding to such art because it makes them feel something and moves them. Knowledgeable collectors are able to find more artists making such work,” Rajagopalan adds.

Both directors see a growing importance for the role of art today, as well as a need for more art appreciation in society. “Artists voice the world’s uncertainty and conflict for us. Engaging with such art reflects your concern about such issues,” Rajagopalan says.

Basu calls on audiences to discuss art with people they meet, attend art events, and visit art galleries. “When you go on holiday, make sure you see a city’s art galleries also,” she suggests.

“And of course, if you are traveling abroad, it is very important to go and see their museums. That is how we can improve art appreciation and knowledge of art right here in India,” Basu signs off.

Now what have you done today to pause in your busy schedule and harness your creative side for a better world?

(All photographs taken by Madanmohan Rao on location at 'Contemporary Now' venues in Chennai.)

item.title: MeitY unveils DEPA handbook to enable trusted data sharing for AI training
item.description: The handbook outlines a techno-legal framework that allows institutions to collaborate on data for AI training while keeping control of their data.
item.content:encoded:
The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) has launched a handbook on Data Empowerment and Protection Architecture (DEPA) for AI training, an official release said Saturday.

The handbook outlines a techno-legal framework that allows institutions to collaborate on data for AI training while keeping control of their data.

IT Secretary S Krishnan unveiled the handbook, which was developed with support from the iSPIRT Foundation, at a roundtable in Bengaluru.

"The framework combines contractual permissions, controlled computing environments and privacy-enhancing safeguards. It also incorporates data provenance, enabling the origin, permissions and use of data to be traced throughout the training process, supporting accountability and transparency," the release said.

As AI becomes central to economic and social development, access to diverse, high-quality data is critical.

Yet concerns around privacy, confidentiality, intellectual property and institutional control often limit data sharing, the release said adding DEPA training addresses these challenges.

"India's AI ambitions must be matched by the ability to use data responsibly and securely," Krishnan said, adding that MeitY is committed to taking the framework forward.

Principal Scientific Adviser Ajay Kumar Sood explained that under DEPA, the model travels to the data rather than the reverse.

He said this enables multi-party and cross-border collaboration, and described DEPA as India's contribution to global science diplomacy.

The roundtable drew representatives from government, industry, academia, research among other stakeholders.

item.title: Weekly VC funding stays subdued at $115M; Prosus gets CCI nod for Navi investment
item.description: Venture capital funding for Indian startups remained subdued through October, with the final week of the month reflecting the continued slowdown in investor activity.
item.content:encoded:
Dear Reader, 

AI investments are beginning to translate into measurable business gains, with companies reporting stronger earnings and improved operational efficiency. Santander said its AI initiatives generated €194 million ($216 million) in business value in the first nine months of 2026, while Novartis and Standard Chartered reported profitability improvements. Meta credited AI with boosting advertising revenue, while Google Cloud’s revenue more than doubled to nearly $31 billion in Q3, highlighting the growing commercial returns from the technology.

Closer home, Dutch investment group Prosus is a step closer to acquiring a stake in Sachin Bansal-led Navi, after the Competition Commission of India (CCI) approved the proposed deal. The approval follows Navi’s $100 million fundraise from Prosus in August, marking the Bengaluru-based fintech’s first institutional capital raise. The deal will deepen Prosus’ presence in India’s digital financial services market.

In other news, Binance says it has replenished approximately 95% of the $6.3 billion in assets stolen in a major security breach, using company funds and reserves. The exchange has begun restoring cryptocurrency withdrawals in phases after completing security checks, while working to source the remaining 5% of less-liquid tokens. Binance has reiterated that users will not bear the financial losses.

Meanwhile, countries at the UN’s COP17 biodiversity summit have agreed on a roadmap to accelerate nature conservation by 2030. The plan calls for reducing harmful subsidies and increasing conservation funding, although a significant financing gap remains a challenge to meeting global biodiversity targets.

In today’s newsletter, we will talk about 

  • Weekly VC funding stays subdued at $115M
  • India needs greater control over app distribution: Indus Appstore and Eloelo   

Here’s your trivia for today: What was the name of the very first internet search engine, created in 1990? (Scroll down for the answer)

Funding

Weekly VC funding stays subdued at $115M

Venture capital funding into Indian startups remained subdued in October, with the absence of large-value deals weighing on overall inflows. The trend continued in the final week of the month, with startups raising $115 million across 29 deals. The largest transaction was a $15 million investment in healthtech startup Cent, while AI startups accounted for two of the deals. As 2026 draws to a close, the funding environment is expected to remain largely unchanged, with hopes of a recovery shifting to 2027.

Key takeaways: 

  • Startups raised $115 million across 29 deals in the last week of October, up from $96 million in the previous week, but large-ticket investments remained elusive.
  • Healthtech startup Cent led the week's transactions with $15 million, followed by AI infrastructure startup Simplismart and AI startup Live2.ai, which raised $14 million each.
  • AI funding activity showed early signs of momentum, with two pure-play AI startups securing investments. However, the broader funding environment is expected to remain subdued through 2026.

TechSparks

India needs greater control over app distribution: Indus Appstore and Eloelo

India’s app-first economy has yet to unlock the full potential of its digital goods market, with distribution barriers and high platform commissions limiting opportunities for developers. At TechSparks 2026, Indus Appstore’s Priya Narasimhan and Eloelo Group’s Sagar Gaonkar argued that India needs greater control over app discovery, distribution and billing. They also highlighted how AI-ready platforms, localised experiences and affordable pricing could help bring the next 500 million users online.

Key takeaways: 

  • India needs a stronger digital goods marketplace, as high commissions of 15–30% charged by dominant app stores make it difficult for developers to sell lower-priced digital products.
  • Digital sovereignty extends beyond chips and AI models to three critical layers: app discovery and distribution, monetisation and billing, and data trust and consent.
  • AI could reshape app discovery and content personalisation, while platforms need to offer locally relevant experiences and flexible pricing to tap India's next 500 million digital users.

News & updates

  • EV Manufacturing: EKA Mobility has expanded its manufacturing footprint with six new facilities across Pune and Pithampur, taking its network to 11 plants with an annual capacity of over 40,000 electric vehicles. The expansion, backed by investments exceeding Rs 3,500 crore, comes as the company reports 1,243% year-on-year growth in H1 FY27 and an order book of over 11,000 buses.  

  • Global EV push: BYD recorded its sixth consecutive month of year-on-year sales growth in October, selling 4.9 lakh vehicles, up 11% from a year earlier. Overseas shipments surged 102.8% to 1.7 lakh units, helping offset sluggish domestic demand and intense price competition in China.  

What you should watch out for

  • The Bengaluru Skill Summit 2026, organised by the Department of Skill Development, Entrepreneurship and Livelihood, Government of Karnataka, will take place from November 3 to 5 at The Lalit Ashok, Bengaluru.

  • Devcon 8, Ethereum’s flagship global developer conference focused on blockchain infrastructure, decentralised applications, Web3 and the future of the Ethereum ecosystem, will take place in Mumbai from November 3 to 6, 2026.

What was the name of the very first internet search engine, created in 1990?

Answer: Archie

item.title: Noel writes to Tata Sons to take biz recast, SP Group’s funding plea at Nov 26 meet
item.description: Noel Tata's letter asks for a discussion on the September 11 letter from RBI, which makes a listing of Tata Sons mandatory by rejecting the application for de-registration.
item.content:encoded:
Noel Tata has written to Tata Sons to take up a business reorganisation plan presented by him to avert listing of the conglomerate's holding company, and Shapoorji Pallonji group's part-exit to raise Rs 25,000 crore at the next board meet scheduled for November 26.

Noel, who chairs Tata Trusts, has sent two separate letters to Tata Sons secretary Suprakash Mukhopadhyay in his capacity as a board member, sources privy to the development said, adding that any member can convey an item to be included in the agenda with 15-day notice.

Emails sent to both Noel Tata and Tata Sons for a response on the development did not elicit a reply immediately.

First of the letters asks for a discussion and a vote on the reorganisation plan, under which it plans to amalgamate Tata Electronic Systems and Tata Consulting Engineers into Tata Sons Private Limited that can help avoid listing the group's holding company, which is considered by RBI as a core investment company and not an operational one.

Noel's letter asks for a discussion on the September 11 letter from RBI, which makes a listing of Tata Sons mandatory by rejecting the application for de-registration. It informs that subsequent to the letter, two of the biggest trusts under Tata Trusts had sent the reorganisation proposal on September 26.

As per the proposal, Tata Sons will become an operating company with the merger of electronics and engineering businesses, and cease to be an NBFC-CIC, which attracts the regulator's listing mandate.

The issue of Tata Sons' listing is core to the differences between Noel and the board of Tata Sons, which outvoted the head of the biggest owner group in the company by favouring for a compliance with the RBI mandate at its meeting on September 17.

Noel's side has been maintaining the need to preserve the character of the over-150-year grouping, advocating that the private character keeps investor pressure on delivering returns at bay and helps it take long term bets. The management of Tata Sons, however, says that it will have to follow the mandate of the regulator.

If the reorganisation plan gets adopted by Tata Sons, the amalgamation proposal will have to get nods from the RBI, National Companies Law Tribunal and also the Central government's Ministry of Corporate Affairs.

The two letters from Noel's side come at the end of a very hectic week, which started with truce talks between Noel and Tata Sons chairman N Chandrasekaran at the former's South Mumbai residence on Sunday. This was followed by a letter from Noel to Tata Sons on Monday challenging Chandrasekaran's reappointment as chairman, and the issue taking a political turn with Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi lambasting the government for interference in the matter.

In the second letter to Tata Sons, Noel seeks information from the Tata Sons management on the progress on the letter from SP Group involving part-exit of its holdings to raise Rs 25,000 crore. He has asked for details on how the proposal has been evaluated and has also presented a draft resolution in the annexure.

item.title: SEBI chairman says market regulator keeping eye on Tata Group developments
item.description: The comments came amid differences over governance matters at Tata Sons, the group's holding company, including the reappointment of N Chandrasekaran as chairman and the question of its proposed listing.
item.content:encoded:
SEBI Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey on Saturday said the market regulator is monitoring developments relating to governance at the holding company level in the Tata Group, and pointed out that the group's listed companies and their promoters are subject to SEBI's disclosure and compliance norms.

The comments came amid differences over governance matters at Tata Sons, the group's holding company, including the reappointment of N Chandrasekaran as chairman and the question of its proposed listing.

"At the holding company level, there are some issues, as that's not really a listed company. The rest of the companies, those which are listed, follow all the LODR (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) norms," Pandey told reporters on the sidelines of the launch of the Bharat Chamber Investors Forum.

These listed companies and promoters of those firms are subject to all norms, he said.

Asked whether the SEBI was keeping track of Tata Group's developments, he said, "Yes... I mean in the sense of, you know, we have to keep monitoring all the developments."

Pandey did not refer to any specific governance violation or regulatory action against the group in his remarks.

The Tata Group has 26 publicly listed companies, with a combined market capitalisation of $328 billion as of March 31, 2025, according to its FY25 annual report.

Of these, seven listed companies collectively hold around 11.92% in Tata Sons, according to an analysis by governance advisory firm InGovern. The firms also have more than 1.77 crore shareholder or folio accounts.

The seven companies are Tata Steel, Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles, Tata Chemicals, Tata Power, Indian Hotels, Tata Consumer Products and Tata Investment Corporation.

These companies are part of the group's larger portfolio of 26 listed entities and represent only those firms identified in the analysis as holding a stake in Tata Sons.

Tata Trusts holds around 66% in Tata Sons, while the Shapoorji Pallonji Group holds approximately 18.4%.

item.title: Policybazaar parent PB Fintech net profit rises 43% rise in Q2
item.description: The revenues for PB Fintech at the end of second quarter of FY27 stood at Rs 2178 crore which was an year-on-year growth of 35%
item.content:encoded:
PB Fintech, the parent company of digital insurance platform Policybazaar and credit aggregator platform Paisabazaar, reported a 42.5% rise in net profit for the second quarter of FY27 while revenue rose by 35% in the same period.

PB Fintech reported a net profit of Rs 192.4 crore in the second quarter of FY27 as compared to Rs 135 crore in the similar period of last fiscal. The revenues for the second quarter came in at Rs 2177.7 crore.

According to the company, it recorded a total insurance premium of Rs 9,385 crore for the second quarter which was a 38% year-on-year (YoY) growth. The core online insurance premium business grew 42% YoY and new health insurance premium rose by 46% YoY. The total lending disbursal by PB Fintech in the second quarter stood at Rs 4,739 crore.

The company has around 5.5 lakh insurance advisors, which grew by 1.3 lakh during the quarter. According to the company, these distributors helped expand insurance access across smaller towns and cities, which contributed to 76 percent of overall gross written premium for the quarter.

This performance comes in the backdrop of Insurance Regulatory Development Authority (IRDA) proposal to lower the commissions earned by insurance agents and this could have an impact on the overall growth trajectory of PB Fintech.

On leveraging artificial intelligence (AI) in its operations, the company said it has 10 crore customer interactions every day. Around 21 lakh calls are processed daily which are 100% AI processed where the talk time exceeds 60 seconds across 7 Indian languages. It does 17 lakh minutes of conversation per day with 8x deeper analysis with AI.

The company processes seven lakh documents per day and this resulted in savings of 1,000 hours daily.

The changes due to AI have seen 15% plus productivity improvement in insurance advisors through AI-driven intent calling and 20% improvement in conversion.

item.title: TVS Capital bets on private credit with Rs 750-Cr fund
item.description: TVS Capital Funds has launched TVS Alts, targeting a Rs 750-crore private-credit fund to provide secured financing to Indian businesses, amid growing demand for alternative lending.
item.content:encoded:
TVS Capital Funds has launched TVS Alts, a private-credit platform targeting Rs 750 crore for its maiden fund, with a Rs 500-crore green-shoe option that could take the corpus to Rs 1,250 crore.

TVS Capital expects domestic capital, including from insurance companies, bank treasuries and corporates. These are potential investors, not confirmed commitments. The proposed fund has been filed with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) and awaits regulatory approval.

TVS Alts plans secured loans of Rs 40 crore to Rs 100 crore to performing companies with sound credit profiles. Such loans are backed by collateral. The fund is targeting returns of about 17% and will support bridge financing, pre-IPO funding for companies preparing to list, and mergers and acquisitions across sectors. 

The investment team has assessed 42 opportunities, with two or three under consideration. It expects a first close within six months of regulatory approval and a final close within 12 to 14 months.

Founded by Gopal Srinivasan in 2007, TVS Capital is a growth private-equity manager focused on financial services and technology. TVS Alts extends its activities from equity investment into lending. TVS Capital owns 90% of the new platform, with co-founder Shyam Srinivasan, Executive Chairman of TVS Alternatives, holding the remainder and spearheading the venture. 

Manish Makaria, previously with TVS Capital and SBI Funds Management, will serve as Managing Partner. 

Srinivasan said the fund would focus on companies with “sound credit profiles, strong underlying fundamentals and adequate security”. TVS Capital recently closed its fourth private-equity fund at nearly Rs 4,000 crore.

The launch comes as private credit becomes an established alternative source of finance in India, although recent deployment has remained broadly steady. EY recorded $3.5 billion in investments across more than 100 Indian deals in the first half of 2026, compared with $3.4 billion in the second half of 2025. 

Domestic funds accounted for 74% of deal value, while transactions worth $10 million to $60 million made up 61%. Refinancing, holding-company funding and acquisitions were among the key uses.

Recent fundraising also reflects growing competition. Kotak Alts closed its Rs 5,000-crore Yield and Growth Fund in September, backed entirely by domestic investors. Motilal Oswal Alternates announced a Rs 1,700-crore first close for its maiden private-credit fund in February. Ascertis Credit Fund IV crossed $700 million in commitments in October.

Meanwhile, the regulatory framework is evolving alongside the market. SEBI amended its Alternative Investment Fund regulations in 2026. The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code was also amended in April to address procedural delays and creditor-related processes, with the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India subsequently consulting on changes to corporate insolvency resolution rules.

item.title: TVS Capital’s Rs 750-Cr private-credit bet; What makes people pay attention to content?
item.description: TVS Capital has launched TVS Alts, a private-credit platform targeting Rs 750 crore, with a green-shoe option lifting its potential corpus to Rs 1,250 crore.
item.content:encoded:
Dear Reader,

The AI gold rush is running into a reality check, and the pressure is beginning to show across technology and crypto.

Anthropic’s much-anticipated Nasdaq debut is facing a tougher road after a week of market jitters over the cost of the AI boom. Its prospectus has impressed investors with reported annual sales growth of 1,300%, but its substantial computing commitments and losses have raised questions about whether surging demand can translate into a sustainable business. 

Earnings from key partners Microsoft, Google and Amazon have added to the uncertainty, with massive infrastructure spending weighing on cash flow, even as cloud growth remains strong. Investors are now weighing the opportunity against the risks, just as Anthropic prepares for a potentially record-setting IPO.

The nerves have also reached OpenAI. According to The Financial Times, the ChatGPT maker has cut its latest funding target by $10 billion to around $20 billion, while lowering its desired valuation to $1.25 trillion from $1.4 trillion. The move comes amid a technology sell-off, with investors becoming more cautious about the huge sums being poured into AI.

Meanwhile, crypto has its own security headache. Following a reported $6.3 billion hack at Binance, rival exchanges including Coinbase and Kraken are strengthening their defences. Executives are also calling for faster information-sharing and coordinated responses, as the industry faces growing pressure to prove it can protect customers and stolen assets.

In today’s newsletter, we will talk about 

  • TVS Capital’s Rs 750-crore private-credit bet
  • What makes people pay attention to content?

Here’s your trivia for today: What was Google’s search engine originally called? (Scroll down for the answer)

Investment

TVS Capital’s Rs 750-crore private-credit bet

TVS Capital has launched TVS Alts, a private-credit platform targeting Rs 750 crore, with a green-shoe option lifting its potential corpus to Rs 1,250 crore. The fund awaits SEBI approval and will lend to performing firms, courting domestic institutions and corporates.

Key takeaways: 

  • The fund plans secured loans of Rs 40 crore to Rs 100 crore, targeting returns of about 17% and financing bridge needs, pre-IPO activity, mergers and acquisitions.
  • TVS Capital owns 90% of the platform, while co-founder Shyam Srinivasan holds the rest and is leading the venture. Manish Makaria has been named Managing Partner.
  • India’s private-credit market saw $3.5 billion invested across more than 100 deals in H1 2026. Domestic funds supplied 74% of deal value, amid fresh rival fundraises.

TechSparks

What makes people pay attention to content?

At TechSparks 2026, leaders from HT Media Labs, Inshorts, and Eloelo Group discussed why credibility, human creativity, and audience-first formats will matter as content creation scales.

The conversation explored how formats shape the way audiences consume content, what makes a format resonate in an increasingly crowded digital landscape, and why the format itself can be as important as the content it carries.

Key takeaways: 

  • Format, distribution, personalisation and the relationship with the consumer are congruent and they co-exist. All of them need to be married in a particular combination to get a person’s attention, said Avinash Mudaliar, Co-founder and CEO of HT Media Labs and the creator of the retro-styled portable music player Saregama Carvaan.
  • Deepit Purkayastha, Co-founder and CEO of digital media and news aggregator company Inshorts, said while AI platforms are increasingly meeting consumers’ on-demand information needs, people still want real-time updates.
  • For GSN Aditya, COO of entertainment tech company Eloelo Group, micro-drama economics have created opportunities to tell stories for more specific audiences rather than chase mass appeal.

News & updates

  • AI training: MeitY launched a DEPA handbook to enable secure, trusted data sharing for AI training, helping institutions collaborate while protecting privacy, intellectual property and data control.
  • Tata Group: SEBI chief Tuhin Kanta Pandey said the regulator is monitoring Tata Group’s governance developments, while stressing that its listed companies must comply with disclosure and regulatory norms.
  • Local production: Omron Healthcare opens its first India factory near Chennai, aiming to boost local production from 300,000 to 3 million units annually and begin European exports by 2027.

Did you know?

What was Google’s search engine originally called?

Answer: BackRub

item.title: Reliance Retail focuses on disciplined JioMart expansion, targets profitability from FY28
item.description: The company is prioritising sustainable growth with investments in dark stores, customer acquisition and margins expected to start contributing positively to profitability from the next financial year.
item.content:encoded:
Country's leading retailer Reliance Retail Ventures Ltd (RRVL) is expanding its dark store network, improving delivery speeds and deepening its presence in smaller cities, while maintaining a sharp focus on unit economics and profitability, said a senior company official on Friday.

The company is prioritising sustainable growth with investments in dark stores, customer acquisition and margins expected to start contributing positively to profitability from the next financial year, as per its roadmap, said Reliance Retail CFO Dinesh Taluja during an earnings call.

It is continuing to scale up its quick commerce operations and build capabilities to respond to evolving market realities, with a focus on developing a hyperlocal network spanning supply chain and technology.

"We are investing right now to build scale in online businesses," said Taluja, adding that the company is "investing in capabilities to improve our availability, improve the speed of delivery, improve reliability".

However, he also said it will grow its scale in e-commerce and quick-commerce with "balanced unit economics". It is maintaining a sharp focus on profitability, including shutting down large-footprint stores that are not performing, while expanding its dark-store network.

In the grocery business, where online revenue has 42% growth in Q2/FY27, a "scale-up of hyperlocal and online visible in revenue mix", it said.

Reliance Retail added 303 new stores in its sales network, with a net reduction of 222 stores after accounting for the closure of unproductive stores.

It has a "ruthless focus" on profitability with shut down on non performing large footprint stores, time lag between this.

"The focus will be on unit economics and not just the number of orders vanity or the reach vanity metrics. The growth will be disciplined with the economics making sense. Wherever the economics don't make sense, we will not grow, and we'll continue to expand our dark store network," he said.

Unlike several online-first competitors that are investing heavily to establish standalone infrastructure, Reliance Retail has an advantage in leveraging its existing physical store network to support online deliveries, he said.

The company has a presence across more than 5,000 stores and operates in over 1,000 cities, providing it with a wider omnichannel footprint than competitors concentrated largely in the top 100 cities.

"We are growing pretty rapidly in the smaller cities as well. There is no competition... Their consumer demand is there, and for us, the incremental costs are much lower," he said.

Taluja said Reliance Retail was witnessing rapid growth in smaller cities, where demand for online grocery services remains largely untapped and incremental infrastructure costs are lower because the company can utilise its existing retail network.

The company has also reported improvements in key operating metrics, he said.

"Our average order values have gone up meaningfully. Our fully fulfilled orders have; the percentage has gone up. The average delivery time has gone down substantially over the last four quarters. So it's all moving in the right direction and with the investment being a credit to the bottom line as well," he said.

Reliance Retail, which had outlined a three- year roadmap, has made substantial progress.

"If you look at growing our JioMart and Omnichannel, we operate the largest Omnichannel network in the country, and that is reflecting in the numbers. We had 42% growth in the online grocery business. B2C grocery market, the share contribution of online has grown to 70 basis points," he said.

Taluja said quick-commerce remains a highly competitive segment, with six players operating in the market, leading to pricing pressure and investments in customer acquisition.

"Our share has grown up by 100 basis points and we operate the largest network of stores. See, if you look at our competition, the next guy is somewhere around 2,500 dark stores," he said.

Reliance Retail is making selective margin investments, particularly in metropolitan areas, to remain competitive and retain customers.

"The good part is, compared to other players who are actually making a loss, we have a profitable core, and we are using that to fund the growth engines, which is the online growth engine, and we're still making money," Taluja said.

The company is also focusing on improving the utilisation of its existing assets and leveraging its scale to enhance margins, rather than relying on discounting-led expansion. Reliance Retail plans to prioritise scale-building for its platform JioMart in FY27 before focusing on profitability and value creation in FY28 and FY29.

The strategy involves expanding JioMart’s reach across platforms and strengthening its omnichannel presence, while improving product availability, delivery speed and reliability.

In FY28 and FY29, the focus will shift towards monetising the expanded business by increasing repeat purchases, average basket sizes and customer lifetime value.

item.title: Binance hit with $6.3B breach; Delhivery reports net profit of Rs 41 Cr in Q2
item.description:
Dear Reader,
Atomberg Technologies is gearing up for its public outing. The smart appliance disruptor has officially secured SEBI's green light to float its initial public offering, blending a Rs 450 crore fresh issue with an offer for sale of over 76.5 million equity shares. Known for transformin
item.content:encoded:
Dear Reader,

Atomberg Technologies is gearing up for its public outing. The smart appliance disruptor has officially secured SEBI's green light to float its initial public offering, blending a Rs 450 crore fresh issue with an offer for sale of over 76.5 million equity shares. Known for transforming the mundane ceiling fan market with energy-efficient BLDC tech, the homegrown consumer tech maker is now preparing to test public market appetite for India's home appliance starups.

The company plans to use the proceeds from the IPO towards debt payment, investments into brand awareness and marketing, R&D and general corporate purposes.

In other news, the government has officially notified the National Social Security Board for unorganised, gig, and platform workers. Tasked with bridging longstanding social safety gaps, the newly-formed board will recommend, formulate, and oversee targeted welfare schemes tailored to the informal workforce.

Established under the statutory framework of the Code on Social Security, this marks a historic shift by integrating digital gig and platform professionals into India's formal welfare architecture, the ministry said.

Meanwhile, in the world of AI, Cursor has uncovered a malicious version of Anthropic's Claude Code extension lurking inside its marketplace, putting as many as 5,000 developers at risk. The compromised release, the version 2.1.313, is a sharp wake-up call to the growing security blind spots in modern AI tooling: as developers race to accelerate workflows, extension ecosystems are quickly becoming high-value targets for attackers.

The 5,000 figure represents potential exposure, not confirmed successful takeovers.

In today’s newsletter, we will talk about 

  • Binance hit with $6.3B breach
  • Delhivery reports net profit of Rs 41 Cr in Q2

Here’s your trivia for today: Which iconic paint manufacturer was founded in a Mumbai garage in 1942 by four friends during the Quit India movement to take advantage of temporary import bans? (Scroll down for answer)

Cryptocurrency

Binance hit with $6.3B breach

Binance has disclosed a massive security breach resulting in an estimated impact of $6.3 billion, with approximately $3 billion worth of digital assets frozen on-chain through coordination with industry partners. 

Preliminary findings indicated the breach began via a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop, granting the attacker access to a service container to execute unauthorised withdrawals. However, subsequent inquiries revealed additional breach points, confirming a much more sophisticated attack than an isolated exploit of a single employee's permissions. 

Key takeaways

  • Binance confirmed there is no evidence that wallet private keys were compromised.
  • The exchange has temporarily suspended withdrawals while undertaking a security revamp of its withdrawal service and related addresses.
  • Assuring customers that their assets remain safe, Binance said it would cover all losses arising from the incident through its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) and the company's own funds.

Delhivery reports net profit of Rs 41 Cr in Q2

Logistics company Delhivery swung to a profit of Rs 40.63 crore during the second quarter of FY27, compared to a loss of Rs 50.49 crore in the same quarter of the previous fiscal year. Revenue rose 19.8% to Rs 3,066.38 crore from Rs 2,559.3 crore in the year-ago period.

  • The company said early investments in AI are also showing results, with improved sales productivity and customer onboarding and faster resolution of claims and disputes and fraud detection.

item.title: Delhivery reports net profit of Rs 41 crore in Q2 of FY27
item.description: The logistics company sees performance improving in the second half of the fiscal year despite the challenges of inflation and labour supply.
item.content:encoded:
Logistics company Delhivery reported a net profit of Rs 40.63 crore during the second quarter of FY27, compared to a loss of Rs 50.49 crore in the same quarter of the previous fiscal year. Revenue rose 19.8% to Rs 3,066.38 crore from Rs 2,559.3 crore in the year-ago period.

Delhivery, in a statement, said it could register a strong performance despite the pressure of inflation.

Express parcel volume recorded a 32% YoY growth touching 325 million shipments for the second quarter. The part truck load segment recorded a 14% YoY growth.

The logistics company said its new businesses are ramping up faster than originally planned.

Delhivery Local, an on-demand, intracity logistics and courier service, is now live across eight cities and is on track to exceed its previous guidance of an annual revenue run rate of Rs 250 crore by Q4FY27, along with improved contribution margins.

Financial Service has also begun early monetisation of its vendor ecosystem, and is developing co-lending partnerships to broaden financial access to vendor partners through an asset-light approach, the company said.

Delhivery said early investments in AI are beginning to bear fruit, with improved sales productivity and customer onboarding and faster resolution of claims and disputes and fraud detection.

Delhivery Robotics, an inhouse automation lab, has commenced production of customised autonomous vehicles for in-facility movement operations. It has also begun testing robotics systems across under-the-roof operations, in partnership with global leaders in the physical AI domain.

Delhivery expressed confidence going into the second half of the fiscal year, despite a volatile macro environment due to rising fuel prices, labour availability issues, and multiple statutory changes. It said its network service levels heading into the festive season have been the best, with improved profitability.

item.title: Two Point O raises $10M led by Transition Venture Capital
item.description: Two Point O will use this funding round to expand into newer asset classes as well deepening its reach in the current energy management segment.
item.content:encoded:
Two Point O Capital (TW.O), an AI-powered, full-stack clean energy deployment platform for commercial and industrial (C&I) businesses, has raised $10 million in a funding round led by Transition Venture Capital. Existing investor Omnivore and angel investors Chiranjeev Singh Saluja and Sudhir M Reddy also participated in the round.

TW.O said it will use the funds to expand into new asset classes, including battery energy storage systems (BESS), and deepen its presence in existing segments such as solar, energy efficiency and wastewater treatment.

The capital will also support its expansion into sectors with significant energy and water requirements, including data centres, automotive, pharma, manufacturing and healthcare, the company said in a statement.

Founded in 2024 by Archit Mehrotra, Karan Bhutani, Manya Ranjan, and Shashidhar Reddy, TW.O helps businesses adopt clean energy infrastructure by bringing together financing, technology and end-to-end project execution.

“This funding will accelerate our vision to become India’s first and largest multi-asset and multi-solution platform enabling adoption of clean energy by C&I customers,” said Karan Bhutani, CEO and Co-Founder of Two Point O Capital.

TW.O partners with OEMs and EPCs across India. Its existing clientele includes the likes of Premier Energies, Godrej, JK Tyre, Morepen Pharma, Wipro, Phoenix Mills, and several other large commercial and industrial customers.

According to the startup, it has grown its assets under management by 1.5x consistently every quarter over the last 3 quarters and uses a proprietary AI/ML-enabled platform for solutioning, underwriting and asset monitoring.

“Two Point O removes the capex barrier, accelerating the adoption of clean energy solutions. The industry often underestimates the complexity of integration across a fragmented ecosystem with multiple stakeholders. By taking end-to-end ownership of execution, Two Point O enables customers to focus on their core business rather than managing the build,” said Yashodhara Bakliwal, VP, Investment at Transition Venture Capital.
